title: Huber fitting gave no clear added East Africa box rain forecast gain in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether Huber regression improves October-December mean rain forecasts for 5 S-5 N, 35 E-40 E. Both models used September rain, Nino 3.4, DMI, and a time trend. Each fit used earlier years from 1979. Across 26 test years in 2000-2025, Huber fitting reduced mean squared error by 7.8% against ordinary least squares. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -7.5% to +35.6%. Thus, the test gave no clear added gain. RMSE fell from 0.7299 to 0.7008 mm/day. Adding DMI within Huber fitting gave a 28.2% point gain, with an interval of -1.5% to +50.1%. This follows a published campaign benchmark and is not an independent confirmation. Revised products, a small region, few years, and conditional intervals limit inference. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure, and independent checks. External source records and annual tables are regenerated outside the signed package.
